decisions.decision: MANUALLY MATCHED tag added, reversing 44-05's original 'operator-picked row carries no tag' rule
decisions.rationale: operator's own words: needed to maintain provenance for data — distinguishing a human decision from an untouched machine suggestion is itself important information, not noise

decisions.decision: sideToggle's highlight stays gated (!gated && side === ...); the fix belongs in seeding sideGateConfirmed correctly, not in bypassing the gate
decisions.rationale: removing the gate check made an untouched row's default side='UNKNOWN' render as Advocate-active, since UNKNOWN !== BENCH — a worse, opposite-direction bug than the one being fixed

decisions.decision: sideGateConfirmed is seeded true only from unambiguous evidence: committedRow.side !== 'UNKNOWN' OR committedRow.person_id != null
decisions.rationale: ArgumentParticipant.side defaults to SideEnum.UNKNOWN, and an operator's own 'confirm generic Advocate, no role yet' action also writes 'UNKNOWN' — the two are genuinely indistinguishable from the stored value alone, so that one case safely re-locks (one extra click) rather than guessing and risking a misleading always-unlocked dropdown

decisions.decision: Extracted side is captured into AdminJob.discrepancies (an untyped list[dict] JSON column) as a new 'extracted_side' key, not a new ArgumentParticipant column
decisions.rationale: no Alembic migration needed, no Pydantic schema change needed (discrepancies: Optional[list[dict]]); captured once in pipeline/commands/resolve.py and pipeline/commands/import_convokit.py at the moment the discrepancy is built, before any operator edit can overwrite ArgumentParticipant.side

decisions.decision: Tenure preview must be a new read-only API endpoint reusing _bench_role_and_missing_tenure, not a client-side reimplementation of the tenure-derivation logic
decisions.rationale: 44-06's explicit prohibition against caching/duplicating the tenure derivation (a tenure-derived role must never be older than the request that rendered it) — a second, drift-prone copy of the logic client-side would violate that same principle even for a 'preview'
